findings.title: Public findMany() method removed with no replacement for ORM-based consumers
findings.body: The previous `findMany(findManyArgs)` method, which returned real Prisma-typed `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` rows via Prisma's ORM query builder, has been removed entirely and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Any other code in the repository that called `InsightsBookingService.findMany(...)` (outside the two files touched by this PR) will now fail to compile/run, since that method no longer exists and callers must switch to writing their own `$queryRaw`/`$queryRawUnsafe` calls. This PR's file list does not include any other call sites being updated, so if production code outside these two files relied on `findMany`, this change silently breaks that integration. This should be verified against all current callers of `InsightsBookingService` before merging.

findings.title: Org-scope authorization condition skips org members when the org has no sub-teams
findings.body: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, `userIdsFromOrg` is only queried when `teamsFromOrg.length > 0`, even though `teamIds` always includes `options.orgId` itself. If an organization has no sub-teams yet (a realistic state for a newly created org), `teamsFromOrg.length` is 0, so `userIdsFromOrg` is forced to `[]` and the membership lookup (which would include direct org members via `teamId = orgId`) is never executed. As a result, org owners/admins viewing insights for an org with zero sub-teams will see no personal (non-team) bookings for any org member, even though they are authorized to see them. This pre-existing logic is unexercised by the new tests (no test covers an org with zero sub-teams), so the bug remains uncaught despite the PR's stated goal of testing 'org scope' authorization thoroughly.

findings.title: Caching behavior tests removed without replacement
findings.body: The previous test suite included a 'Caching' describe block that verified `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` correctly cache and reuse computed conditions (`cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions`). This PR deletes that entire block and does not add any equivalent coverage for the Prisma.sql-based implementation. The caching fields/logic still exist in `insightsBooking.ts` (`cachedAuthConditions`, `cachedFilterConditions`), but there is now no test verifying that repeated calls reuse the cached `Prisma.Sql` value rather than rebuilding (and re-querying the database) on every call, which is a meaningful regression in test coverage for a performance-sensitive code path.

findings.title: Constructor options type weakened, loses compile-time validation of discriminated union
findings.body: The constructor parameter type changed from `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (the zod-inferred discriminated union, which requires `teamId` only for `scope: "team"`) to the looser `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is always optional regardless of `scope`. This means TypeScript no longer catches a caller constructing the service with `scope: "team"` but omitting `teamId` at compile time; it now silently fails zod validation at runtime and falls back to `NOTHING_CONDITION`, hiding the mistake until it is observed as unexpectedly empty insights data rather than a type error during development.

findings.title: PR description misstates scope of changes, downplaying risk in reviewed service file
findings.body: The PR description states the service (`insightsBooking.ts`) was 'previously converted' to Prisma.sql and that this PR only updates the integration tests to match. However, the actual diff shows the service file itself undergoing the Prisma.sql conversion in this same PR (removing `findMany`, changing the constructor's option type, rewriting all authorization/filter condition builders from ORM objects to raw SQL). This mismatch between the stated scope and the real diff could cause reviewers to under-scrutinize the higher-risk service-layer SQL/authorization logic, assuming it was already reviewed and merged separately.
